rationale: Three lenses ran against the implementation diff (src/ + tests/). Two blocking findings: (1) GET /v1/info can 500 when the DB is unavailable because get_deployed_at has no try/except while startup treats the same failure as non-fatal; (2) docstring/success log still claim (APP_VERSION, ENV) after the environment column was intentionally removed. Deferred 3 (first-deploy-only semantics by design, IntegrityError return-None at startup unused, Optional vs server_default pattern). Dismissed 4 false positives (lifespan call site present, downgrade present, broad except matches local pattern, duplicate-index style).

findings.title: GET /v1/info can 500 when DB is unavailable
findings.problem: get_deployed_at() has no try/except. Startup treats DB failure as non-fatal (deployed_at stays null), but app_info() calls get_deployed_at() unguarded, so the same outage returns HTTP 500 on /v1/info.
findings.impact: Breaks the non-fatal contract advertised for this feature and can fail a previously resilient public info endpoint when Postgres is down or the table is missing.
findings.recommendation: Wrap get_deployed_at (or the router call) in try/except, log a warning, and return None so /v1/info still returns 200 with deployedAt: null.

findings.title: Docstring and log still claim ENV scoping after environment column removal
findings.problem: _initialize_deployment_version docstring and success log refer to (APP_VERSION, ENV) / env={config.ENV!r}, but DeploymentVersion and the migration unique only on version with no environment column.
findings.impact: Operators are misled about multi-env / shared-DB behavior: the same APP_VERSION across environments sharing one DB collapses to a single deployed_at row.
findings.recommendation: Update docstring and log to version-only wording (drop ENV), or restore environment column + unique(version, environment) if env scoping is still required.
